choice: _config_cap gives factory.md's low cap only when the intake_risk row says low and the polled ticket.risk says low; anything else is the high cap
why: #195 stores the intake risk; a missing row is unknown and unknown is never low; a Linear ticket whose labels or files cannot be read this poll is high for that poll without being stored, so dropping ticket.risk would under-cap it

choice: lib/intake_risk.py owns the table name, schema and read; the dispatcher creates it in _initialize and the poller's IntakeRisks uses the same schema
why: lib/poll_source.py imports lib.dispatcher, so the dispatcher cannot import poll_source; one shared module keeps one schema

choice: _effective_cap opens one connection and passes it to _config_cap; resume passes its open transaction's connection
why: reads cap_extra and the stored risk on the same connection, inside the caller's transaction when there is one

choice: tests that hand the dispatcher a low ticket now seed the stored low through IntakeRisks, as the poller does; test_risk_once's cap checks run over a stored low
why: a low ticket with no stored risk is now high by design; the T18a checks prove ticket.risk high wins even over a stored low

choice: tests/test_cap_from_stored_risk.py polls a brief risk=low then a builder ready risk=high through LivePollSource into the dispatcher database and reads the review job's round 1/1
